html: The Kichwa of the Tigre River are an Indigenous people of the Tigre basin in Loreto, northern Peru, near the Ecuadorian border. They speak a lowland form of Quechua. Quechua was spread here in colonial times by missionaries and traders as a common language, and peoples of different origins, among them Zaparoan groups related to the Arabela, came to speak it. From the 1970s oil companies drilled in the Tigre and nearby river basins, and decades of spills polluted their rivers and fish; Peru declared environmental emergencies there in the 2010s. Related communities live on the Pastaza.
